roster.label: Starting Lineup
roster.value: 1 QB, 2 RB, 2 WR, 1 TE, 3 FLEX (RB/WR/TE), 1 SUPERFLEX (QB/RB/WR/TE)

team_blurbs.Wanghaf: The Ferrari with no glovebox. 25 players — the smallest roster in the league — and somehow every single one is good. #1 in Power Rankings, but one bad bye week from finding out just how thin that roster really is.
team_blurbs.Jaron: Consistently excellent, rarely the center of league chat drama. The dynasty equivalent of a reliable sedan — #2 overall, and about as exciting to talk about as one.
team_blurbs.Cope: Best starting lineup in the entire league, full stop. That said, the bench looks like it was built from whatever was left over after everyone else drafted — one injury to a starter and this whole thing gets shaky fast.
team_blurbs.Bway: The receiver room here is borderline unfair — best WR1 and WR2 in the league, plus the best FLEX2. Just don't look too closely at what's happening at QB and TE, because it's not pretty.
team_blurbs.Zach: Solidly top-half in dynasty value, which makes it worse that the season projection has this roster near the bottom of the actual standings. Great assets, rough Sundays incoming.
team_blurbs.White P: Two separate trades, two fresh mouths to feed at RB and WR — while everyone else argued about it in the group chat, the shelves quietly got restocked. Worth noting: not one of those new pieces was actually drafted here.
team_blurbs.Cdonn: The league's most prolific trader, for better or worse — and lately 'worse' is looking like the early leader. All that trade volume hasn't actually moved the roster up the rankings.
team_blurbs.Jack Mehoff: Jahmyr Gibbs headlines a starting lineup with the best RB1 and S-FLEX in the league. Everywhere else on the roster, though, it falls off a cliff — sitting at #8 overall isn't a fluke.
team_blurbs.LBS7: First in league chat volume by a wide margin, with plenty of roster moves to match the energy. Problem is, all that activity has landed this team at 9th — loud doesn't always mean good.
team_blurbs.Bryce Tall: Currently propping up the standings with the league's weakest starting lineup. On the bright side, last place comes with the best draft position next year — silver linings, or at least a decent excuse.

news_posts.title: Welcome to the 2026 Season
news_posts.body: The site's live — Power Rankings, Standings, Head to Head, the whole thing. It's Week 0, so most trackers are sitting at zero, but that'll change fast once games kick off. Wanghaf enters as the Power Rankings favorite with the shallowest-but-strongest roster in the league, while Jack Mehoff projects as the early favorite to actually win games behind the league's best RB1. Check back every Tuesday for the weekly recap once results start rolling in.
